##### KEKERASAI.I

# CHAPTER I

## GENERAL PROVISIONS

#### Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency is Musi Rawas Regency;

2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Rawas Regency; 4
3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Rawas.
4. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
5. Elimination of Domestic Violence is a guarantee provided by the state to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence, prosecute perpetrators of domestic violence, and protect victims of domestic violence.
6. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of the person holding control over that other person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
7. Victim of Trafficking in Persons is a person who experiences psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering, caused by the criminal act of trafficking in persons.
8. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, economic, psychological to the victim.
9. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds, or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death
10. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

11. Sexual violence is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

12. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
13. Women in contact with the law are women in conflict with the law, women as victims, women as witnesses or women as parties.
14. Child is a person under the age of 18 years, including those in the womb.
15. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
16. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
17. Guardian is a person or body that in reality exercises custodial power as a parent over a child.
18. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
19. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental impairment so as to interfere with his/her growth and development properly.
20. Child with excellence is a child who has extraordinary intelligence, or has special potential and/or talent.
21. Adopted child is a child whose rights are transferred from the environment of the authority of the family of parents, legal guardian, or other person responsible for the care, education, and raising of that child, into the family environment of the adoptive parents based on a court decision or determination.
22. Foster child is a child who is cared for by a person or institution, to be given guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, because his/her parents or one of his/her parents is unable to guarantee the child's proper growth and development.
23. Custody is the power of parents to care for, educate, maintain, foster, protect, and develop the child in accordance with the religion professed and the ability, talent, and interest.
24. Rights of the child are part of human rights that must be guaranteed, protected, and fulfilled by parents, family, community, government, and the state.
25. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
26. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate, optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
27. Special protection is protection given to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic, and other addictive substance abuse (napza), children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of abuse and neglect.
28. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is, or has occurred.
29. Victim recovery is all efforts to empower victims of domestic violence to be more empowered both physically and psychologically.
30. Implementation of Recovery is all actions that include services and assistance to victims of domestic violence.
31. Recovery implementation officer is a health worker, social worker, volunteer companion, and/or spiritual counselor.
32. Companion is a person who has the expertise to accompany victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
33. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the empowerment of victims of domestic violence to resolve the problems faced.
34. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, based in hospitals, managed jointly in the form of medical services (including medico-legal), psycho-social and legal services.
35. Cooperation is a systematic and integrated manner among recovery implementers in providing services to recover victims of domestic violence.
36. Safe house is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with established operational standards.
37. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.
38. Every person is an individual or corporation.
39. Household is family members, relatives (grandchildren, nieces/nephews, older siblings, younger siblings, grandfathers, grandmothers, cousins and so on) and non-relatives (servants, drivers and so on) who live and eat from one kitchen and reside in one house.
